checks.what: Linear Pottery loss to nobody in -4940 of the Alföld cells that ledger event 7 misses. The page says the classical Alföld culture of the LBK "flourished until about 4940". That matches the year, and event 7 of the dossier uses the same year and the same counterpart, nobody. The spec resolves to 54 cells: Pest 22, Bihor 28, and the city units of Szeged, Szolnok, Kecskemét and Békéscsaba 1 each. In both anchors, data/anchors-c/m5000 and m4900, the Linear Pottery holds exactly 11 of these cells and the other 43 belong to no one, so the loss changes only the 11 specks. The 6 Pest cells lie at lon 19.36-19.95, east of the Danube, in the Pest plain and not in Transdanubia. The Bihor cell is at 21.57E 46.69N, on the plain edge. No other Linear Pottery cell remains in the Alföld box (lat 45.3-48.8, lon 19-23.5) at m4900, and no other cell remains in the Hungarian city units (Debrecen, Nyíregyháza, Miskolc, Eger, Hódmezővásárhely, Budapest). The patch therefore clears the whole problem it names. The spec takes in more land than the specks (all of Pest and all of Bihor, including hills), but the Linear Pottery holds nothing in that extra land and the gazetteer has no Alföld region to narrow it with, so it does no harm. The Linear Pottery regains nothing in the ledger after -4940, only losses down to the dissolution in -4500, so no other year changes. --check-patch: ok.

problems: Not a patch error, for the dossier owner only: the same page says the classical Alföld culture "descended into" the Szakálhát-Esztár-Bükk local groups, which it dates "about 5260–4880". This could argue for an Alföld end nearer -4880 than -4940. The patch rightly follows ledger event 7's -4940, which the page states directly.
